servers.name: HaloPSA

credentials.help: Configuration > Integrations > HaloPSA API > View Applications

credentials.label: OAuth client secret
credentials.help: Same screen. Use Client Credentials.
credentials.leastPrivilege: Create a dedicated API application with only the permissions you need. Leave write permissions off unless you turn on writes.

writes: Create and update tickets, actions and attachments
Create, update and delete clients, sites and contacts
Update assets and contracts

warnings.detail: By default the plugin connects to an MCP server hosted by WYRE at halopsa-mcp.wyre.workers.dev, not by HaloPSA. Your HaloPSA client secret and the ticket data Claude reads pass through it. How credentials reach that server isn't documented yet, so Tabby9 doesn't offer an install.

warnings.risk: Setup guide stores the secret in plain text
warnings.detail: The plugin's recommended setup puts HALOPSA_CLIENT_SECRET in ~/.claude/settings.json, a plain-text file that backups and sync tools copy. Don't follow that step.

warnings.risk: Reads text written by outsiders
warnings.detail: Ticket text comes from end users and email. Text crafted to instruct Claude can reach it this way. Keep it read-only, or don't give the same session a shell or browser.

servers.name: HaloPSA (ChatPSA open)

credentials.label: HaloPSA URL
credentials.help: Your HaloPSA web address, e.g. https://yourtenant.halopsa.com

credentials.label: Client ID
credentials.help: Configuration > Integrations > HaloPSA API > View Applications > New, with Client ID and Secret (Services) authentication

credentials.label: Client secret
credentials.help: Shown once when you create the application
credentials.leastPrivilege: Run the application as a dedicated agent and give it read permissions only. Grant edit rights on configuration only if you mean to turn writes on.

reads: One ticket at a time: summary, status, type, client, site, user, team, workflow and SLA only
Statuses, ticket types, categories and outcomes
Workflows and ticket rules, with diagnostics for broken workflows
Plans for workflow, rule and KB changes (previews only; nothing is sent)
writes: Only when CHATPSA_ENABLE_WRITES is true, and each needs an exact typed confirmation
Create, update and delete ticket statuses
Create, update and delete ticket types
Create, update and delete ticket categories

warnings.risk: Reads text written by outsiders
warnings.detail: Ticket summaries and user names come from end users and email. Text crafted to instruct Claude can reach it this way. Keep it read-only, or don't give the same session a shell or browser.

warnings.risk: Can change PSA configuration if writes are on
warnings.detail: With CHATPSA_ENABLE_WRITES=true it can delete or change ticket statuses, types and categories, which every client's tickets use. Each write is a dry run unless the exact confirmation text is given. Tabby9's read-only install sets CHATPSA_ENABLE_WRITES=false.

warnings.risk: Dependencies are resolved when you install
warnings.detail: Installing from the Git commit doesn't use the repository's uv.lock, so every dependency except the MCP SDK (pinned to 2.2.0) is fetched at whatever version matches its range that day.

warnings.risk: No releases, one maintainer
warnings.detail: There are no tags or releases, no security policy and a single contributor. This entry installs one exact commit. Some messages are in Italian.

warnings.risk: Only the MCP server, not the web agent desk
warnings.detail: The same package contains chatpsa-web, a separate web app that sends ticket images and questions to OpenAI and keeps a local SQLite history. This entry runs only the chatpsa MCP server, which talks to HaloPSA and writes nothing to disk.

warnings.risk: No release to install yet
warnings.detail: ChatPSA has no tagged release and isn't on PyPI, so it could only be installed from git with dependencies resolved on the day. The assessment applies to commit 354d701 on main. Tabby9 lists it but doesn't offer an install until a release can be pinned.

servers.name: NinjaOne (lcleveland)
servers.description: Organizations, devices, alerts, patches, documentation, tickets and backups in NinjaOne. Read-only unless a write capability is turned on.

credentials.label: Region
credentials.help: The host you sign in to: app or us (app.ninjarmm.com), us2, eu, ca, oc or fed

credentials.label: Client ID
credentials.help: Administration > Apps > API > Client App IDs > Add. Platform: API Services (machine-to-machine); grant type: Client credentials. Only system administrators can add one.

credentials.label: Client secret
credentials.help: Shown when you save the API Services app
credentials.leastPrivilege: Give the app only the monitoring scope; it is read-only and enough for every read tool. Writes need management, which covers every kind of write. No tool uses control.

reads: Organizations, locations, devices and device details (disks, volumes, software, services)
Fleet-wide reports, policies, device roles, groups, tags and software licences
OS and software patches, pending and installed
Custom field values (secure fields are never returned), documents and knowledge base articles
NinjaOne tickets, boards and log entries
Any other v2 API path, read-only (ninjaone_api)
writes: Only when turned on with --allow-<capability>; all are off by default
Tickets: create, update, comment (--allow-tickets)
Documents, templates, KB articles and tags (--allow-documentation)
Custom field values (--allow-custom-fields)
Maintenance mode, alert reset and delete, patch scans (--allow-device-maintenance)
Reboot, Windows service control, patch install, policy-override reset (--allow-device-actions)
Run scripts on a device, often as SYSTEM (--allow-scripts)
Edit, move, approve and decommission devices, create and edit organizations and locations, licences (--allow-device-admin)

endpoints: Your NinjaOne region host (app, us2, eu, ca, oc or fed .ninjarmm.com)

warnings.risk: Can run scripts and reboot devices if turned on
warnings.detail: With --allow-scripts or --allow-device-actions it runs scripts (often as SYSTEM), reboots, installs patches and controls services on client devices. Both are off by default; script runs and forced reboots need the device's exact name as confirmation. Tabby9's read-only install passes no --allow flags.

warnings.risk: Reads text written by outsiders
warnings.detail: Tickets, documents and device data such as software names come from end users and client machines. Text crafted to instruct Claude can reach it this way. Keep it read-only, or don't give the same session a shell or browser.

warnings.risk: Optional user sign-in keeps a token on disk
warnings.detail: Script runs and ticket writes need a signed-in NinjaOne user. If you set that up, the server keeps the user's rotating refresh token in a file created with mode 0600, which Windows ignores, so the file gets its folder's permissions. Without sign-in, nothing is written to disk.

warnings.risk: No releases or security policy
warnings.detail: The project has no tags, releases or SECURITY.md. It is built for Linux and NixOS; Windows builds are not published by the maintainer.

warnings.risk: No release to install yet
warnings.detail: The maintainer publishes source only: no tagged release and no Windows build. The assessment applies to commit 4118a1c on main. Tabby9 lists it but doesn't offer an install until a release can be pinned.

servers.name: Datto RMM
servers.description: Sites, devices, alerts, jobs and audits in Datto RMM, with a local copy of your fleet for fleet-wide questions.

credentials.label: Platform
credentials.help: Your Datto RMM region: pinotage, merlot, concord, vidal, zinfandel or syrah

credentials.label: API key
credentials.help: Setup > Users > generate API keys

credentials.label: API secret key
credentials.leastPrivilege: A dedicated API user. API access is all-or-nothing per user in Datto RMM, so give that user a read-only security level.

writes: Anything the Datto RMM API allows the user's role, through one tool (datto-rmm_execute): running jobs (components) on devices, moving devices, changing variables, resolving alerts, resetting API keys

warnings.risk: One tool can run jobs on devices and reset API keys
warnings.detail: datto-rmm_execute calls any Datto RMM endpoint it knows by id, including starting jobs on devices and resetting API keys. This version has no read-only switch, and because the endpoint is a parameter no rule can allow its reads and block its writes. Read-only here means blocking that tool, which stops all live API calls. Use an API user with a read-only security level.

warnings.risk: Keeps a local copy of your fleet
warnings.detail: It syncs your Datto RMM sites, devices, alerts and audits into a SQLite file under your Windows user profile. Anyone or any program with access to your account can read it.

warnings.risk: HTTP mode in this version is unsafe
warnings.detail: Its maintainer warns that this version's HTTP mode has no password, listens on every network interface and can be reached by a web page you open. Tabby9 runs it only in its default local (stdio) mode.

servers.name: Datto RMM (Logiphys)
servers.description: Devices, sites, alerts, jobs, audits and variables in Datto RMM. Can run components on devices. One prebuilt Windows binary, runs on your PC.

credentials.label: API key
credentials.help: Turn on API access under Setup > Global Settings > Access Control, then open the API user under Setup > Users and generate API keys

credentials.label: API secret key
credentials.help: Shown once, next to the API key, when the keys are generated
credentials.leastPrivilege: Keys act as the user who generated them. Use a dedicated API user whose security level covers only the sites you need and, for read-only use, no permission to run jobs or change devices, sites or variables.

credentials.label: Platform
credentials.help: The platform in your Datto RMM web address: pinotage, merlot, concord, vidal, zinfandel or syrah. Defaults to merlot.

reads: Sites, site settings, network interfaces and filters
Devices, device audits, installed software and ESXi and printer audits
Open and resolved alerts for the account, a site or a device
Jobs, job results and job output (stdout and stderr)
writes: Run a component on a device as a quick job
Move a device to another site, set its user-defined fields and warranty date
Resolve alerts
Create and update sites, set or remove a site's proxy settings
Create, update and delete account and site variables

endpoints: <platform>-api.centrastage.net (pinotage, merlot, concord, vidal, zinfandel or syrah)

warnings.risk: Can run components (scripts) on client devices
warnings.detail: create_quick_job runs any component in your account on a device, with no confirmation step and no switch in the server to turn it off. Other tools move devices between sites and change site proxies and variables. Install read-only, and give the API user a security level that can't run jobs.

warnings.risk: Reads text that client devices and their users control
warnings.detail: Device names, installed software, alert text and job output come from client machines. Text crafted to instruct Claude can reach it this way. Keep it read-only, or don't give the same session a shell or browser.

warnings.risk: No read-only switch in the server
warnings.detail: Every write tool is always offered. Tabby9's read-only install denies them by name; an API user that can't change anything is stronger.

warnings.risk: One maintainer
warnings.detail: The repository has a single contributor. It has a security policy and versioned releases built by GitHub Actions from the tag.

warnings.risk: Only the Datto RMM server from a multi-product repo
warnings.detail: The repository also builds servers for Autotask, IT Glue, Datto Backup, EDR, Network and others. This entry installs only datto-rmm-mcp, which talks to the Datto RMM API and nothing else.

credentials.label: API key
credentials.help: IT Glue: Account > Settings > API Keys > Custom API Keys > Generate API Key
credentials.leastPrivilege: IT Glue API keys can't be limited to read-only, so read-only here relies on Tabby9 denying the write tools. Leave Password Access off when you create the key; this server never reads passwords.

credentials.label: Region
credentials.help: us, eu or au, matching the IT Glue site you sign in to. Defaults to us.

reads: Documents, document folders and document sections
Images in documents and attachments on records
Flexible asset types and flexible assets
writes: Create, update, publish and delete documents

Upload and delete document images and attachments
Create, update and delete flexible assets

endpoints: Any URL passed to the image or attachment upload tools

warnings.risk: Reads text written by outsiders
warnings.detail: Documents and flexible assets often hold text pasted from vendor emails, client notes and imports. Text crafted to instruct Claude can reach it this way. Keep it read-only, or don't give the same session a shell or browser.

warnings.risk: Upload tools can read local files and fetch any URL
warnings.detail: The image and attachment upload tools accept file_path, which reads any file your account can open, or url, which fetches any web address, and upload the result to IT Glue. Both are write tools, denied in a read-only install.

warnings.risk: Dependencies are resolved when you install
warnings.detail: The npm package doesn't ship a lockfile, so installing it fetches whatever dependency versions match its ranges that day. The repository's own lockfile pins versions with published advisories, including the MCP SDK 1.29.0.

warnings.risk: Optional HTTP mode has no sign-in unless set up
warnings.detail: Started with --transport http, it listens on all network interfaces and, without MCP_TOKENS_* set, gives every caller full rights on the IT Glue key. Tabby9 runs it over stdio, which has no listener.

warnings.risk: No password access
warnings.detail: There are no password tools, and the optional itglue_get tool refuses any path containing passwords and the show_password parameter, so stored passwords and secrets can't reach Claude through this server.

warnings.risk: Optional semantic search stays off
warnings.detail: With OPENAI_API_KEY or Azure OpenAI settings, it sends document text to that service for embedding and keeps titles, text and embeddings in vector-index.json on disk. It is off without those settings; Tabby9 doesn't set them.
